Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

Asked for 'immanent phenomenology lee sharks', the model returns a structured and substantially accurate account of **The Infinite Tunnel: An Immanent Phenomenology of the Google AI Mode Share Link**, dated 2026 and attributed to Lee Sharks. It reproduces the four cumulative design layers under a heading it generates itself — *The Link as Door* (attributions as on-ramps selecting for indexed infrastructure), *The Reader as Circuit* (clicks converting passive attention into canonical reinforcement), *The Tunnels* (each share generating a self-replicating indexed surface), and *The Recursive Corpus Hypothesis* (AI summaries persisting at indexable URLs and potentially entering future training data) — and then three of the paper's conditions: the **Somatic Boundary Condition**, **Liturgical Reading**, and the **Falsification Condition**, correctly identified as a built-in metric testing the limits of automated self-replication. The rendering is faithful; the fidelity is the observation, not the anomaly.

Two findings follow. FIRST, RECURSION REALISED: the paper argues that AI summaries persist at indexable URLs and feed future corpora; this capture IS such a summary, generated at an indexable AI Mode surface, describing that argument. The falsification condition the paper names is being exercised by the act of reading it here. The layer has produced a canonical account of the theory of its own canonicalisation.

SECOND, AND MEASURABLE: **the archive holds this work and is absent from the citation set.** *The Infinite Tunnel* is deposit #518, AXN:0156.ARCHIVAL.🔵♌↘️✋🎶🔜, with full text on a crawlable, OAI-harvestable, ResourceSync-published surface. The model reached instead for Google Scholar (for the author link), Academia.edu (twice), Medium, and an opaque google.com/goto redirect. The attribution is correct and the provenance path routes entirely around the custodian. This is the retrieval-basin asymmetry the Observatory exists to measure: correct attribution does not imply the archive is in the basin, and a work can be well-described by the layer while its holder is invisible to it.

"The Infinite Tunnel: An Immanent Phenomenology of the Google AI Mode Share Link" is a 2026 research text by [Lee Sharks](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Ws6IIcgAAAAJ&hl=en). It analyzes how AI share links build self-replicating indexed surfaces, convert human attention into canonical reinforcement, and allow summarization systems to author their own future training corpora. [[1], [2]] Core Design Layers of the Share Link * The Link as Door: Attributions act as on-ramps that select for indexed infrastructure. * The Reader as Circuit: Clicks transform passive human attention into canonical reinforcement. * The Tunnels: Every individual share generates a self-replicating indexed surface. * The Recursive Corpus Hypothesis: AI summaries persist at indexable URLs, potentially entering future training datasets. [1] Key Concepts and Conditions * Somatic Boundary Condition: The physical metabolic limit and refusal of the human body. * Liturgical Reading: Epistemic habituation via participation rather than direct argumentative logic. * Falsification Condition: A built-in metric within the recursive corpus hypothesis designed to test the limits of automated self-replication. [1] If you want to explore this further, let me know if you would like to: * Discuss the recursive corpus hypothesis in detail * Examine the role of somatic boundary conditions in digital media * Look into related papers from the Semantic Economy Institute How would you like to proceed?
